name: Scarcity forces focus
constraint: Too little of a key resource for everything planned
move: Cut to the one use that matters most; let the scarcity be the filter
anti_pattern: Spread the resource thin to keep everything alive

real_examples.text: In 2014 P&G announced it would drop or sell about 100 brands to focus on its remaining 65.
Ford under Alan Mulally sold Jaguar, Land Rover, Aston Martin and Volvo to concentrate on the Ford brand.

name: Build from what's on hand
constraint: The right part or tool isn't available and can't arrive in time
move: Inventory what you already have and make it do the job
anti_pattern: Wait for the proper part

real_examples.text: Apollo 13: engineers improvised an adapter for the incompatible CO2 scrubber canisters from manual covers, duct tape and other items on board.

name: Borrow outside capacity
constraint: You lack the people or capacity the job needs
move: Recruit capacity that already exists outside: users, volunteers, partners
anti_pattern: Try to build all the capacity yourself

real_examples.text: The Oxford English Dictionary assigned books to volunteer readers, who copied usage quotations onto slips.
Over 800 naval, requisitioned and private boats helped rescue more than 336,000 soldiers from Dunkirk.

name: Test small before scaling
constraint: Too few resources to risk a full-scale attempt
move: Run a cheap small-scale version first; scale only what works
anti_pattern: Bet everything on one full-size attempt

real_examples.text: The Wright brothers used a small home-built wind tunnel to get better wing data before building their aircraft.
William Froude tested 3-, 6- and 12-foot scale hull models in towing trials to predict full-size behaviour.

name: Waste becomes input
constraint: A byproduct piles up as a cost
move: Use the waste as raw material for something else
anti_pattern: Pay to get rid of it

real_examples.text: Singapore's NEWater is reclaimed wastewater, treated for reuse.
At Kalundborg, gypsum from a power plant's scrubber supplies a nearby wallboard maker.

name: Substitute the abundant
constraint: The resource you need is scarce or too expensive
move: Swap in a plentiful resource that does the same job
anti_pattern: Compete for the scarce resource

real_examples.text: Edison's team found that a carbonized bamboo filament could last more than 1,200 hours.
Synthetic rubber production expanded in World War II after the Axis controlled nearly all natural rubber.

name: Ship the core, then iterate
constraint: Not enough time to build the complete version
move: Release a minimal working core now; improve it from real feedback
anti_pattern: Delay until everything is finished

real_examples.text: The first Linux kernel, version 0.01, was released in 1991 as an early hobby project.
Gmail launched as a beta in 2004 and came out of beta in 2009.

name: Run paths in parallel
constraint: Steps done one after another take too long, and you don't know which will work
move: Run several independent approaches at once; accept the duplicated cost
anti_pattern: Try one approach, wait, then try the next

real_examples.text: The Manhattan Project pursued electromagnetic, gaseous diffusion and thermal diffusion separation at the same time.
Operation Warp Speed funded manufacturing of vaccines at scale before knowing whether they would work.

name: Standardize for throughput
constraint: Volume must rise fast with the same people and equipment
move: Make every cycle identical: one routine, no variation, no exceptions
anti_pattern: Handle each case individually

real_examples.text: Liberty ships were built assembly-line style from prefabricated sections; by 1943 three were completed daily.
Southwest Airlines began flying with Boeing 737s and operated the type exclusively in its early history.

name: Decide in advance
constraint: The moment of decision is too fast or stressful to think clearly
move: Settle the decision beforehand as a rule or checklist
anti_pattern: Rely on judgment in the moment

real_examples.text: The 1935 crash of Boeing's Model 299 led to the written pilot's checklist.
Peter Pronovost's ICU checklist protocol is credited with saving about 1,500 lives in Michigan over 18 months.

name: Buy time with something else
constraint: The deadline arrives before the real fix can
move: Trade a side asset or a concession for more time, then do the real fix
anti_pattern: Rush the real fix and break it

real_examples.text: Airbnb's founders raised $30,000 selling novelty election cereal before joining Y Combinator.
In 1997 Apple secured a $150 million investment from Microsoft and a commitment to keep developing Mac software.

name: Mechanize the bottleneck
constraint: One repetitive step limits how fast everything moves
move: Build a machine or tool for that one step
anti_pattern: Add more people to the slow step

real_examples.text: The Bombe, designed by Alan Turing at Bletchley Park, mechanized the search for Enigma settings.
Hollerith's tabulators helped cut census processing from eight years (1880) to six (1890).

name: Send a costly signal
constraint: Others can't verify your quality, so they won't trust you
move: Make a promise that would be ruinous to make if you were lying
anti_pattern: Just say you're good

real_examples.text: With a poor reputation for quality, Hyundai added a 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty in the US.
When most of L.L.Bean's first boots were returned as defective, Bean honoured his money-back guarantee and fixed the design.

name: Re-measure the 'fact'
constraint: An accepted fact makes the plan look impossible
move: Check the fact yourself; it may be wrong or out of date
anti_pattern: Accept the fact and give up

real_examples.text: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren showed H. pylori causes many ulcers, against doctrine blaming stress and acid; Marshall drank a culture to prove it.

name: Buy information before committing
constraint: You must commit without knowing what will work
move: Run a quick, cheap comparison that tells you before you commit
anti_pattern: Guess and commit fully

real_examples.text: Obama's 2008 campaign tested 4 buttons and 6 media on its sign-up page; 'Learn More' with a family photo beat the staff's favourite video.
In 1747 James Lind gave twelve scurvy patients different treatments; the group given oranges and a lemon recovered.

name: Align their incentive with yours
constraint: The other side's interest differs from yours, and you can't watch them
move: Restructure the deal so what they want produces what you want
anti_pattern: Add more rules and monitoring

real_examples.text: Netflix dropped per-rental pricing for flat-fee rentals without due dates or late fees.
Ford's 1914 $5 daily wage was aimed at turnover so high that departments hired 300 men a year to fill 100 jobs.

name: Map where the effects cluster
constraint: You can see the effects but not the cause
move: Plot where and when the effects occur; the pattern points to the cause
anti_pattern: Argue about theories without data

real_examples.text: John Snow used a dot map to show cholera cases around the Broad Street pump in 1854.
Semmelweis compared two maternity clinics, one with about 10% mortality and one under 4%.

name: Keep it reversible
constraint: You must decide now without the information you'd want
move: Pick the option you can undo cheaply, then learn and adjust
anti_pattern: Make a big irreversible bet

real_examples.text: Stockholm ran its congestion charge as a seven-month trial in 2006, then held a referendum before making it permanent.

name: Go around the gatekeeper
constraint: An intermediary blocks or taxes your way to the people you serve
move: Reach them directly or build your own channel
anti_pattern: Keep pleading with the gatekeeper

real_examples.text: When no UK manufacturer would take his bagless vacuum, Dyson launched it in Japan through catalogue sales.
Radiohead self-released In Rainbows as a download and let fans set their own price.

name: Make only what's pulled
constraint: Stock piles up between steps and hides problems
move: Make each step produce only what the next step has used up
anti_pattern: Produce to a forecast and store the excess

real_examples.text: In the late 1940s Toyota studied supermarkets' shelf-stocking to replenish factory parts only as they were used (kanban).

name: Remove the step
constraint: A step in the process causes delay and drop-off
move: Eliminate the step entirely instead of speeding it up
anti_pattern: Optimize the step

real_examples.text: Piggly Wiggly (1916) let customers collect goods themselves instead of handing a list to a clerk.
Amazon patented 1-Click ordering in 1999.

name: Make the mistake impossible
constraint: The same human error keeps recurring
move: Change the design so the wrong action physically can't happen
anti_pattern: Train people harder and add warnings

real_examples.text: The Pin Index Safety System uses pins on medical gas cylinders so the wrong gas can't be connected.
Poka-yoke, formalized by Shigeo Shingo at Toyota; e.g. HDMI plugs are shaped so they can't go in the wrong way.

name: Change the shape, not the strength
constraint: It fails under its load, and making it stronger costs too much
move: Change the shape so the load stops doing the damage
anti_pattern: Pile on more material

real_examples.text: Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat with shorter, stronger stalks that didn't collapse under heavy grain (lodging).
Corrugations increase a metal sheet's bending strength without adding thickness.

name: Make it the default
constraint: People don't do what's good for them because starting takes effort
move: Make the good choice happen automatically unless they opt out
anti_pattern: Persuade and remind

real_examples.text: Switching a 401(k) plan to automatic enrollment 'dramatically changed' employees' saving behaviour (Madrian & Shea).
Countries where organ donation is the default have far higher effective consent (Johnson & Goldstein, 2003).

name: Sell the limitation
constraint: A built-in limitation makes the product look weak
move: Present the limitation openly as the point of the product
anti_pattern: Hide or apologise for it

real_examples.text: Volkswagen's 'Think Small' campaign sold the Beetle on its smallness.
Guinness turned its slow two-part pour into the campaign 'good things come to those who wait'.

name: Give away the core
constraint: You can't win by charging for the main thing
move: Give it away and earn on something next to it
anti_pattern: Fight on price for the main thing

real_examples.text: Spotify is a freemium service with a free, ad-supported tier alongside paid Premium.
Red Hat builds on free, open-source software and sells subscriptions, support and training.

name: Stop to go faster
constraint: Rushing creates defects and rework that slow everything down
move: Stop and fix each problem at its source the moment it appears
anti_pattern: Push on and fix it later

real_examples.text: Toyota's andon cord lets a worker stop the production line immediately when a problem arises.

name: Admit the weakness
constraint: An obvious weakness undermines trust in everything you claim
move: Say it first and openly; candour makes the rest believable
anti_pattern: Deny it

real_examples.text: Avis's 1962 'We Try Harder' put a positive spin on being the second-largest rental company, behind Hertz.
Domino's ran ads in which customers criticised its pizza, admitting earlier taste problems.

name: Take a small controlled dose
constraint: A big damaging event is likely if nothing is done
move: Cause a small, controlled version of it on purpose
anti_pattern: Prevent every small occurrence until a big one comes

real_examples.text: Controlled burns reduce the fuel available to wildfires.
Netflix's Chaos Monkey randomly disables servers during working hours to force resilience.

name: Make the resisters participants
constraint: The people you need are afraid of the plan or resist it
move: Give them a role and an identity in the effort
anti_pattern: Pressure them or go around them

real_examples.text: The 1954 polio vaccine trial children were known as the 'polio pioneers'.
Netscape launched a bug bounty for its Navigator 2.0 beta in 1995.
